fields.System.Title: INV-9 — Availability projection
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Answer "how much of this can I sell?" in one indexed read instead of an aggregation across
thousands of balance rows.

Scope

In. Maintaining, rebuilding, and reconciling product_availability.

Out. Using it for allocation. Never. See below.

Design notes

The honest query is expensive. Summing available quantity across all sellable locations,
excluding quarantine, damaged stock, blocked locations, and expired batches, means scanning
many rows and joining to locations and batches. Fine occasionally. Not fine when the webshop
asks for two hundred products every few seconds.

Update it synchronously, in the same transaction as the movement. Availability is one of
the few projections that cannot tolerate staleness measured in seconds.

Never allocate from it. This is the rule that matters most in this feature. A projection is
for looking, not for promising. Reservations read the real balance under a lock. Reading a
projection to decide whether to promise stock is how you sell the same unit twice.

INV-902 ships with INV-901, not after it. During an incident you need to run the
rebuild, not write it. And testing the rebuild against the incremental update is the only way
to discover that the two disagree — which they will, quietly, until someone checks.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Projection used for allocation | [doc 09 §12](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Projection drifts from source | [doc 08 §10](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Rebuild disagrees with incremental update | [doc 08 §5.2](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Staleness invisible to consumers | [doc 08 §5.3](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
